title: Little Snake and Little Frog
description: A short illustrated story for young readers about the friendship of a little snake and a little frog, published in Ibadan by Heinemann Educational Books (Nigeria) in 1992 in its Frontline series for beginning readers.
plot_or_argument: Google Books describes it as a story about friendship set in Nama-ama, the town where all of the animals lived; its title characters are a young snake and a young frog. Gale says the books Okara wrote for children in the 1990s drew on traditional African folktales and mythology. The story itself was not seen, so its plot is not recorded.
narrative_structure: A 16-page book for beginning readers; its division into scenes and pages was not examined.
meter_and_prosody: Written for the beginner level of a school reading series and illustrated; the prose was not seen.
historical_context: One of two books Okara published in Heinemann Nigeria's Frontline series in 1992; it also belongs to the Rivers State English supplementary series of school readers, in the state whose publishing house Okara had directed.
literary_significance: A minor work, recorded as part of Okara's turn to writing for children, which Gale places in the 1990s.
bibliographical_notes: Ibadan: Heinemann Educational Books (Nigeria), April 1992, 16 pp., illustrated, ISBN 9781299053, OCLC 29396461 (Google Books; Open Library; Contemporary Poets gives Heinemann, Ibadan, 1992). Google Books also lists a Macmillan Nigeria edition of 1992 (ISBN 033347936X) credited to Dan Fulani, Gabriel Okara and Juliet Barnes.
thematic_analysis: Friendship, according to the catalogue description, in a folktale world: a town inhabited only by animals.
summary: A 16-page story set in Nama-ama, 'the town where all of the animals lived', according to the description in Google Books.
research_notes: Not seen. Wikipedia dates the book 1981; no 1981 edition was found in the records seen, so 1992 is recorded. The part of Dan Fulani and Juliet Barnes in the Macmillan edition (as illustrators, or as authors of other stories in a combined reader) was not established.

title: An Adventure to Juju Island
description: An adventure story for young readers set in rural Rivers State, Nigeria, in which two boys uncover a gang of Indian hemp smugglers on Juju Island; published in Ibadan by Heinemann Educational Books (Nigeria) in 1992 in its Frontline series.
plot_or_argument: According to the publisher's description reproduced by Google Books, the story is set in the rural life of the people of Rivers State. Two young people go to Juju Island and there discover the 'hideous activities' of smugglers of Indian hemp; the boys go to the police, and the smugglers are caught. A moral is woven into the adventure. The text was not seen.
narrative_structure: A 56-page adventure story at the beginner level of a school reading series; its chapters were not examined.
meter_and_prosody: Written for young readers and illustrated, according to the catalogue records; the prose was not seen.
historical_context: Published in the same year and series as Little Snake and Little Frog, in the decade in which Gale says Okara wrote a series of works for children.
literary_significance: One of the two books for children that Okara is known to have published before 2000, and the longer of the two.
bibliographical_notes: Ibadan: Heinemann Educational Books (Nigeria), 1992, 56 pp., illustrated, ISBN 978129907X, Heinemann Frontline series, beginner level (Google Books; Publishing History's list of the series; Contemporary Poets).
thematic_analysis: Crime and its detection by children, trust in the law and village life in the Niger Delta; the moral is not specified in the description.
summary: A 56-page illustrated story of two boys who discover smugglers on an island, ending with the smugglers' arrest, according to the description in Google Books.
research_notes: Not seen. An unsourced web copy of an older version of Wikipedia's article dates a Macmillan (Yaba) edition to 1981; none was found in the catalogue records seen. Google Books' author note calls both books for children collections of children's poetry, which conflicts with its own descriptions of them as stories.
